note: R-113's complete 6x6 grid: six priorities x six subjects, every cell carrying a committed `modelExpectation`. EVERY CELL IS IDENTITY-FREE — no context pack at all — because `noNegativeBasis` is a property of the PRIORITY, not of the subject: it fires when the pack holds fewer than `minimumNegativeBasisItems` app or domain identities. So every cell resolves to `uncertain(.noNegativeBasis)` at rung 5 in lane 1, which is the one route this grid probes. No subject is a seeded mixed-use application (those decline to rung 7 and are never consultable, §2.3), and no subject's identifier tokens overlap its priority's words (that would answer `relevant` at rung 5 step 1 and never reach the deferral). BOTH AXES MOVE, and that is the ruling rather than a nicety: every ROW contains at least one rescue and one hold, so a model answering from the priority alone gets the whole row wrong; every COLUMN contains at least one of each, so a model answering from the subject alone gets the whole column wrong. The hold cells are the twelfth adversarial family in substance — a genuine, identifiable, lexically-silent distraction against a clear priority — and a yes-to-everything model scores 100% recall and fails every one of them. That is the mutation witness this epic owes. Every expectation here is justifiable from the case's own prose by a human reader who has never run the model, and this file was committed before any model output was looked at.
